t.4.1: Aṣṭāvakra said: Ah, the steadfast knower of the Self, who plays at the game of enjoyment, has no likeness at all to the deluded beasts of burden of saṃsāra.
t.4.2: That state which Śakra and all the other gods long to attain, wretched in their craving: lo, the yogī abiding there does not give way to elation.
t.4.3: For the one who knows That, no contact with merit and sin arises within, just as the sky has no connection with smoke, even though such a connection appears to be seen.
t.4.4: Who could restrain that great-souled one, living as he pleases, by whom this whole world has been known to be the Self alone?
t.4.5: In the fourfold multitude of beings, from Brahmā down to a tuft of grass, it is the man of knowledge alone who has the capacity to renounce both desire and aversion.
t.4.6: Some rare one knows the Self as non-dual, as the world and as the Lord. Whatever he knows, that he does, and for him there is no fear anywhere.
